subject: Re: International model fit — follow-up and prompt starter pack
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Müller <sandra.mueller@linguedu.de>, Kenji Saito <ksaito@tokyoai.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Multiregion fit discussion

Hi Sandra / Kenji —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: improve EU + APAC lang coverage for LinguEdu’s tutor-asst product (German, Polish, Spanish, Japanese, Thai).
- Success metrics: per-locale human rating >= 4.0/5 on knowledge & fluency, latency <= 350ms p50 for chat flows, and <5% hallucination rate on knowledge checks.
- Constraints: prefer open models / manageable licensing; tight latency targets for EU region.

High-level model fit recommendations (first pass)
- EU languages (DE/PL/ES): try a 2-tier approach — a larger dense variant for high-quality long-form answers (e.g., 70B-class optimized and quantized) + a responsive 13–30B chat-tuned variant for interactive tutoring.
- APAC (JA/TH): prioritize encoder-decoder or Japanese-optimized models for polite-form handling and tokenization; add an explicit morphological post-process step for Thai.

Attachments I’m sharing now
- linguedu_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (starter prompts + evaluation prompts per locale)
- benchmark_summary_eu_apac.xlsx (quick benchmark runs we ran on similar workloads)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Would you run the attached prompt set against a sample of 200 transcripts (we can supply) and flag high-failure prompts? — Sandra/Kenji
2) If agreed, we’ll propose a 60-day pilot: Dedicated trial capacity + per-locale evaluation harness (we’ll provide the harness).
3) Internal: Neha will recommend exact model builds and quantization profiles; Marcus will scope latency/cost estimates.

I’ll follow up with a concrete pilot SOW and costs by Friday.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: linguedu_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (42 KB), benchmark_summary_eu_apac.xlsx (110 KB)

From: Sandra Müller <sandra.mueller@linguedu.de>

Date: 2028-08-10T15:05:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Multiregion fit discussion

Tessa —

Thanks for the clear recap and materials. A few quick clarifying questions from our side after the call:

1) For Polish we’re particularly sensitive to diacritics and morphological agreement — do you have any runs showing word-error or token-level dropout for pl_PL? I glanced at the benchmark spreadsheet but want a short summary.
2) For Japanese, our product uses polite and casual modes depending on learner level — can the prompt set toggle that reliably?
3) Licensing: if we pick a 70B-class open model, what does the pilot pricing look like for 60 days?

We’ll start a quick run of the prompt set against 120 sample dialogues later this week and share the failures; do you want them posted to the Drive link?

Appreciate it —
Sandra Müller
Head of Product, LinguEdu

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Müller <sandra.mueller@linguedu.de>, Kenji Saito <ksaito@tokyoai.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Multiregion fit discussion

Sandra — good questions. Answers below plus an updated ask.

Quick answers
- Polish: summary from the benchmark sheet — on our sample (1.2M tokens across dialogue-turns) pl_PL had token dropout concentrated on diacritics in 2.3% of tokens; surface-form errors (agreement/case) were ~4.1% for the mid-sized models and <2% for the larger 70B quantized run. I’ll paste a short excerpt below from the run.
- Japanese: the prompt set contains explicit instruction tokens to toggle "polite" vs "casual" styles. We recommend a small post-prompt finite-state check to ensure verb endings match the desired style for sensitive flows.
- Pricing: pilot estimate in a separate SOW draft — ballpark for Dedicated trial (70B-class quantized) is $X/month (I’ll attach SOW).

Excerpt from benchmark (sample):
- pl_PL: diacritic dropout ~2.3% (most common: ó, ł, ś) at 512-token contexts on 30B variants.
- de_DE: compound noun splitting errors in long technical answers ~3.8% on 13B chat-tuned.
- ja_JP: polite/casual mismatch detected in ~6% of single-turn prompts when we didn’t include explicit style tokens.

Proposed next actions (concrete)
1) LinguEdu runs the attached prompt_set against 120 transcripts and uploads failures to the Drive link. We’ll triage and tag by failure mode (fluency / hallucination / style). — Sandra/Kenji
2) Redwood provides a short A/B config (70B quantized vs 30B-chat) and a runbook for the pilot harness. We’ll instrument per-locale eval metrics (BLEU + human rating + hallucination tagging). — Neha
3) Joint kickoff: target start 2028-09-04, 60-day run, sample size ~10k tokens/day.

I’m attaching a small test harness (pilot_test_harness.tar.gz) that includes the eval runner and instructions. If you prefer, we can also host the harness and run the trial for you under Dedicated trial capacity.

Thanks — looping Neha/Marcus for model/cost details.

—
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Attachments: pilot_test_harness.tar.gz

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sandra Müller <sandra.mueller@linguedu.de>
Date: 2028-08-12T16:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: International model fit — follow-up and prompt starter pack

Thanks — quick internal addendum and proposed config matrix. Keeping this short for the thread: 

Model/config suggestions (per locale)
- EU (de_DE, pl_PL, es_ES):
  * Primary: Open70B-OPT-q4 (quantized) — best quality/price tradeoff for long answers.
  * Fast fallback: Chat-30B-mt (chat-tuned) — lower cost, acceptable for interactive sessions.
  * Prompt engineering: include explicit token: "[LOCALE:pl_PL] [STYLE:formal]" as part of the system prompt for forms.

- APAC (ja_JP, th_TH):
  * Primary: JP-optim-34B-encdec (encoder-decoder family) for polite forms and better tokenization.
  * Fallback: Chat-13B-ja (lightweight chat-tuned) with a Thai post-processing tokenizer.

Quantization / latency notes
- Use q4_0 for the 70B-class in Dedicated (preserves most of the FLOP efficiency while keeping hallucination down in our tests).
- Expect p50 latencies ~320–420ms for 70B quantized depending on sequence length; Chat-30B p50 ~180–240ms. Marcus, please confirm cost delta per 1M tokens for the customer pilot.

Evaluation plan / acceptance criteria
- 60-day pilot; success = per-locale human rating >= 4.0 and <3% critical hallucinations on knowledge checks; otherwise roll to alternate model variant or increase Dedicated throughput.

I’ll draft the SOW + a short model runbook and drop both to the Drive link tonight. Tessa — can you confirm LinguEdu’s sample size and whether they prefer Redwood-run or self-hosted harness?

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Applied ML | Redwood Inference
